title: Commodity decision record
description: The commodity swarm's terminal machine record — written by .claude/agents/commodity/commodity-thesis/99_commodity-thesis-synthesis.md to commodity/runs/<COMMODITY>/decision_record.json. This is the commodity-scoped twin of the research swarm's decision_record.json (frameworks/DECISION_LEDGER.md §5) — a smaller shape, but NOT one exempt from CLAUDE.md §10. It used to be: the record deliberately omitted a scenario/forecast ledger on the grounds that a single-verdict dossier did not need one. That was wrong under §23 (a module may add detail, never relax a root standard). The dossier already states a bear-case price (key_levels.support and the cost-curve orb's bear fair value), which is exactly the condition §10 attaches its requirements to — probabilities that sum to 100, an expected return that reconciles to Sum(probability x return), a stated risk/reward, a time window, and a falsification trigger per forecast. Without them the dossier could use probability-weighted LANGUAGE while carrying no distribution (the GOLD dossier's 'that is not today's probability-weighted reality' is the case in point) and no forecast the §19 ledger could ever grade. scenarios[]/expected_return_pct/downside_risk_pct/risk_reward/scenario_horizon_days below close that, reusing the research swarm's field names verbatim so one consumer reads both. Validated by scripts/validate_screener_json.py --fixture (schemas_root, per .claude/agents/commodity/SWARM.md), whose check_commodity_scenario_math is the commodity-scoped twin of eval.py check M.

calibration_feedback.description: Additive — the Phase 2 shape above is otherwise preserved unchanged. The commodity-scoped twin of the research swarm's Phase 6 calibration-feedback gate (frameworks/DECISION_LEDGER.md §18): 99_commodity-thesis-synthesis.md reads the latest commodity/performance/<DATE>_calibration_summary.json dated on/before decision_date and, where this commodity's own calibration_by_commodity slice shows poor calibration OR a commodity/performance error_taxonomy_distribution category is leading and undefended, applies a bounded confidence haircut and records the check here (whether or not it fired) — never omitted once a qualifying calibration summary exists. Required going forward by scripts/validate_screener_json.py's commodity-scoped twin of eval.py check AG, not by this schema (an older run genuinely predating the gate has nothing to report).

source_summary.description: path to the as-of commodity/performance/<DATE>_calibration_summary.json used, or null if status is 'not_available'.

haircut_points.description: 0 unless status=='applied', in which case the fixed constant (8), mirroring the research swarm's own bounded haircut.

flagged_slices.description: commodity ids whose calibration_by_commodity slice triggered the haircut via the hit-rate trigger; [] unless status=='applied'.

leading_error_categories_flagged.description: Additive (error-taxonomy extension, mirrors the research swarm's leading_error_categories_flagged): the error_taxonomy_distribution category names from the as-of summary (count >= 2) whose error_defense_evidence entry is the literal admission 'no defense evidence found'. []  unless a category flagged. Records dated before the error-taxonomy extension omit it; treat absence as [].

error_defense_evidence.description: Additive (error-taxonomy extension): an object keyed by every leading error_taxonomy_distribution category (count >= 2) in the as-of summary, whether or not it ends up flagged. {} when the as-of summary has no leading category yet, or when no calibration summary exists at all. Records dated before the error-taxonomy extension omit it.

rationale.description: one or two sentences naming the as-of summary's verdict and, when checked, this commodity's hit-rate/N numbers and/or any leading error-taxonomy category that flagged on an admitted 'no defense evidence found' — plain enough that a reviewer can verify the haircut without opening the calibration summary.

confidence_haircut.description: Additive — written by scripts/commodity_pre_mortem_haircut.py (commodity:full step 5.5 / commodity:rerun step 6.5) after that run's pre_mortem*.json completes. original `confidence` minus post_review_confidence_score, derived from the pre-mortem's recommended_confidence, never trusted as a possibly-zeroed self-reported field (mirrors the research swarm's fix F28). 0 when the call survives the pre-mortem clean. Absent on a run whose finish-gate has not yet run (a pre-existing run awaiting its first backfill, or a run this schema predates).

pre_mortem_verdict.description: Additive — the latest pre_mortem*.json's `verdict` verbatim ('Survives' / 'Survives with haircut' / 'Does not survive — downgrade' / 'Thesis broken'), copied in by the same finish-gate step. Absent when the finish-gate has not yet run.

post_review_confidence_score.description: Additive — the confidence the engine actually stands behind after its own red-team: the pre-mortem's recommended_confidence when a finish-gate has run, else absent. `confidence` above is the synthesizer's original, PRE-pre-mortem number and is never overwritten (CLAUDE.md §18/§22 — caps are applied, never silently overridden); calibration and review consumers should prefer this field when present, mirroring scripts/calibrate.py's confidence_of() preference for the research swarm.

post_mortem_action.description: Additive — `action` above, capped by the pre-mortem's recommended_action_cap when the finish-gate ran and a cap was warranted (never a LESS cautious value than `action` — commodity:pre-mortem.md rule 1); equal to `action` when no cap fired or the finish-gate has not yet run. commodity:review.md and any calibration consumer should prefer this field over `action` when grading the call the engine actually holds, mirroring scripts/calibrate.py's basket_of() preference for the research swarm.

scenario_horizon_days.description: Additive (§10 'every forecast has a time window'). The horizon EVERY scenarios[] return_pct and price_target below is measured over — one window for the whole distribution, so the probabilities are commensurable. Commodity theses are typically tactical (90-180 days); state the window the catalyst chain actually resolves over, not a convenient round number. Required once scenarios[] is present.

scenarios.description: Additive (CLAUDE.md §10 / §19). The bear/base/bull distribution the dossier's fair-value band already implies, made explicit and machine-checkable: probabilities sum to 100, and expected_return_pct must equal Sum(probability/100 x return_pct). Field names are the research swarm's verbatim (frameworks/DECISION_LEDGER.md §5) so calibration and review consumers read one shape across swarms — with `invalidated_if` added, because a commodity forecast's falsification trigger is what /commodity:review grades it against later (§19). price_target is in the benchmark's own units (the unit named in current_price), NOT a per-share price; return_pct is measured from current_price.value over scenario_horizon_days.

scenario_id.description: stable slug, unique within the record — the id /commodity:review cites when grading this case

label.description: must map onto the cost-curve orb's own bear/base/bull band — the distribution and the fair-value band are one object, not two

return_pct.description: position return over scenario_horizon_days, measured from current_price.value. Roll-adjusted where the stated expression is a roll-bearing vehicle — a contango carry cost is part of the return, not a footnote (the GOLD dossier priced ~3.5%/yr of roll drag and then omitted it from the call).

price_target.description: the benchmark level this case resolves to, in current_price.unit

conditions.description: what must hold for this case, each observable and dated where the driver is a scheduled release

source.description: §5 citation for the levels and conditions — the orb or primary source they came from

joint_probability_basis.description: required as a non-empty explanation when several INDEPENDENT conditions must hold at once (a conjunction is less likely than its parts); null when the case turns on one condition

invalidated_if.description: §10 falsification trigger: the observable that would prove THIS case wrong, checkable without re-running the thesis. Not the negation of `conditions` restated — a real, dated tripwire.

expected_return_pct.description: Additive (§10). Sum(probability/100 x return_pct) across scenarios[], over scenario_horizon_days. Machine-reconciled by check_commodity_scenario_math — a hand-typed number that disagrees with its own distribution fails, so the arithmetic cannot drift from the prose.

downside_risk_pct.description: Additive (§10). The bear case's return_pct — the loss the call accepts if the bear resolves. Signed the same way as return_pct (negative for a long that loses).

risk_reward.description: Additive (§10 'risk/reward is stated where a bear-case price exists' — which a commodity dossier's bear fair value always is). expected_return_pct / |downside_risk_pct|, or the bull/bear ratio where the dossier states it that way; either convention is fine as long as the record and the prose agree.

data_needs.description: Optional, forward-looking. External data series whose absence caps this run's conviction (§11) — surfaced on the cockpit 'Data needs' dock so a durable connector can be built to feed them in continuously. The synthesizer emits the NEED (what / why / where it plugs in / a suggested source); the connector's implementation spec (endpoint, output schema, host allowlist) is authored later by the human at the approval/dispatch step, never here. A `filing_required` need is advisory only — no connector can satisfy it. Omitted or empty when nothing external is capping the call.

need_id.description: stable slug, unique within the run (connector idempotency key)

series.description: the missing data series in plain words, e.g. 'USDA WASDE US wheat ending stocks-to-use'

why_it_caps.description: why its absence limits conviction, tied to the §11 sufficiency read

cap_lifted.description: what sharpens once the series feeds in (optional)

filing_required.description: true = only a statutory filing can close this gap; a connector/scrape can NEVER satisfy it (structurally non-dispatchable). false = connector-eligible.

entry_modules.description: the module(s) that consume this series — they drive the scoped rerun when it arrives

name.description: the best source — an official / public-domain body preferred (USDA, NOAA, CFTC, an exchange) over a redistributor

licensing.description: known licensing / ToS note, or 'public_domain' (optional at emit; the human confirms it at approval)

tier.description: §4 source-tier ceiling this series can earn — NEVER 1-4 (a live feed is not a filing). An API / vendor feed is 5; a dated web scrape is 9 or 10.
